newsitem.title: CENTRAL AFRICAN REPUBLIC: Fresh Bangui clashes as mediator starts talks.
newsitem.headline: Fresh Bangui clashes as mediator starts talks.

text.p: Fresh clashes broke out in the Central African Republic capital Bangui on Thursday as newly returned Malian mediator Amadou Toumani Toure began talks to try to broker a ceasefire, witnesses said.
Spokesmen for African peacekeepers and for disaffected soldiers blamed one another for starting the clashes, during which the two sides exchanged automatic arms fire.

Toumani Toure, Mali's widely respected former military leader, brokered a January 25 peace deal to end three army mutinies in under a year. Officials said he launched his latest talks with a meeting of the follow-up committee he presides.
Clashes broke out on June 20 after an incident involving peacekeepers and a group of soldiers among those who had yet to rejoin their units under the January deal.
Red Cross officials say the clashes have killed at least 80 people, many of them civilians.

Mutinies in April and May 1996 in Bangui began as pay protests but evolved into a bid to topple President Ange-Felix Patasse, a civilian from the north, elected in 1993. A third mutiny began in November and degenerated into ethnic bloodshed.
